title: Minimum Suffix Flips
statement: Start from a string `s` that has the same length `n` as the binary string `target` but holds only `'0'` characters. One move picks an index `i` (`0 <= i < n`) and inverts every character of `s` from position `i` through position `n - 1`, so each `'0'` becomes `'1'` and each `'1'` becomes `'0'`. Return the fewest moves after which `s` equals `target`.
constraints: Every character of target is '0' or '1'
notes:
## Intuition

A flip at index `i` changes positions `i` and later, never anything to its left. So walk from left to right: when position `i` is reached, everything before it is already right and only a flip that starts exactly at `i` can fix `i` without breaking them. Every flip therefore happens exactly where the bit we need differs from the bit the earlier flips left there. After an odd number of flips the rest of `s` reads `'1'`, after an even number it reads `'0'`, so a flip is needed exactly where `target` changes from one character to the next (counting an imaginary `'0'` before the start). Simulating the flips directly costs O(n²); counting the changes costs O(n).

## Approach

1. `current` is what the remaining part of `s` holds right now; it starts as `'0'`.
2. For each `bit` of `target` from left to right, if it differs from `current`, one flip must start here: add 1 to `flips` and set `current` to `bit`.
3. Return `flips`.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = "10111"`, `current = '0'`. The first `'1'` differs, so `flips = 1` and `current = '1'`. The `'0'` differs, so `flips = 2`, `current = '0'`. The next `'1'` differs, so `flips = 3`, `current = '1'`. The last two `'1'`s match. The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `target`.
- Space: O(1): a counter and one character.

## Pitfalls

- A leading `'1'` needs a flip too, because `s` starts as all zeros; start `current` at `'0'`, not at `target[0]`.
- Do not actually flip the suffix each time; that is O(n²) for alternating strings.
- Counting the `'1'` characters is wrong: `"111"` needs one flip, not three.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `flips` | number of flips used so far |
| `current` | the character every not-yet-checked position of `s` holds now |
| `bit` | the character of `target` being checked |

narration.3: s starts as all zeros, so every position after the checked part currently reads '0'.
narration.4: Check target from left to right; earlier positions are already correct.
narration.5: The character here does not match what s holds now.
narration.6: Only a flip starting exactly here fixes it without disturbing the left part.
narration.7: That flip changes everything from here on to this character.
narration.10: Each change in target needed exactly one flip; return the count.
